title: Unbounded atom interning — cap the table, route the three untrusted vectors through a fallible intern, and stop lying about the limit
purpose:
Ground: finding M7 of the 2026-07-23 whole-repository review (`docs/REVIEW-23-07.md:86`, reviewed at beamr `fd71c5e`). Queue position: RF-002 follows RF-001 (the ETS match-spec allocation abort, which is the top of the dispatch queue) and sits alongside RF-003 in the untrusted-input DoS band the review groups as priority 4. One root cause, three reachable vectors: the atom table interns without any ceiling, leaks every name permanently by design, and reports a limit it does not enforce. The consequences are a permanent unbounded memory leak from a remote peer or from ordinary BIF calls in a loop, and — if the process lives long enough — a `u32` index wrap that would silently alias distinct atoms. Real BEAM caps the table (`+t`, default 1,048,576) and refuses loudly rather than growing forever.

RE-PIN AT a0359a2 (review line numbers checked against current main):
- ROOT: `crates/beamr/src/atom/table.rs` — `pub fn intern(&self, name: &str) -> Atom` at `:220`; the review's cited `:228` is `let index = self.next_index.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);` inside `intern`'s `Entry::Vacant` arm — STILL AT `:228`, no drift; the `Box::leak` is `:230`. `next_index: AtomicU32` declared `:189`. The struct doc at `:181-185` states the leak is deliberate: "runtime atoms are never freed in this design, which lets `resolve` return a borrowed `&str`".
- THE LIE: `pub const fn limit(&self) -> usize { u32::MAX as usize }` at `:266-270`. It is surfaced to Erlang code: `Scheduler::atom_limit` (`crates/beamr/src/scheduler/mod.rs:1835`) → `SystemInfoFacility::atom_limit` (`crates/beamr/src/native/system_info_bifs.rs:86`, dispatched at `:131`/`:246`) → `erlang:system_info(atom_limit)`. So the VM reports a finite ceiling of 4,294,967,295 that nothing checks.
- VECTOR (a) DISTRIBUTION, review cite `control_link.rs:267` → STILL `crates/beamr/src/distribution/control_link.rs:267`, `let term = decode_term(control_etf, &mut context, atom_table)?;` inside `decode_control_addressed` (fn at `:259`). MATERIAL CLARIFICATION: that line is the reachability point, not the intern; the actual uncapped intern is one level down at `crates/beamr/src/distribution/etf.rs:627`, `fn decode_atom` → `Ok(Term::atom(atom_table.intern(name)))`. ALSO: there is NO `safe` parameter anywhere in beamr's distribution decoder — the review's "`safe=false`" is describing OTP's `binary_to_term/2` `safe` option by analogy. The builder must not go looking for a flag to flip; the decoder is unconditionally interning.
- VECTOR (b) BIFs, review cite `native/gate3_bifs/type_conversion.rs:51` → EXACT, no drift: `bif_binary_to_atom` (fn at `:44`) ends `Ok(Term::atom(table.intern(name)))` at `:51`. Its sibling, uncited by the review but the same defect: `bif_list_to_atom` at `:112`, interning at `:120`. Both are one process call away from any user code. (`binary_to_existing_atom` `:78-83` and `list_to_existing_atom` `:124-135` use `lookup` and are already safe.)
- VECTOR (c) LOADER: `crates/beamr/src/loader/decode/budget.rs:10` already caps `MAX_ATOMS_PER_MODULE: usize = 65_536` PER LOAD and charges it at `DecodeBudget::charge_atom` (`:61-69`). That is a per-module budget, not a global one — N module loads still intern N × 65,536 atoms with no global ceiling.
- VOCABULARY GAP: there is no `system_limit` atom anywhere in the tree (grep for `system_limit`/`SystemLimit` across `crates/` returns zero hits). `COMMON_ATOMS` (`atom/table.rs:101-179`) has exactly 77 rows at stable indices 0..=76, `Atom::INFINITY = Self(76)` being the last.
- HOUSE PRECEDENT for the shape of this fix: `crates/beamr/src/loader/decode/budget.rs` — hard ceilings as plain documented `const`s, charged through small fallible `charge_*` methods that return a typed error, with no runtime knob. This brief extends that doctrine from the loader to the atom table.
- BLAST-RADIUS FACT the design must respect: `.intern(` appears at ~1,378 call sites across the workspace, the overwhelming majority in tests and in code interning compile-time-known names. Making `intern` fallible workspace-wide is not a one-lane change.
task:
DESIGN STANCE (decided, one fork carved as OQ-A): cap the table, make the cap enforceable only through a NEW fallible entry point, route the three untrusted vectors through it, and give each vector a refusal in its own existing error vocabulary. `intern`'s signature does not change and the ~1,378 trusted call sites are NOT rewritten. "Halt loudly" is realised as a typed refusal at each seam plus a truthful `atom_limit` — NOT as a node abort (see D5).

D1 THE CONSTANT AND THE FIELD. `ATOM_TABLE_LIMIT: usize = 1_048_576` — a plain documented `const` in `atom/table.rs`, house style per `budget.rs`. Provenance to state in the doc comment: this mirrors ERTS's documented default maximum atom count (the `+t` emulator flag); the builder must CONFIRM that figure against the `erl` manual at build time and record the confirmation in the handoff rather than inheriting it from this brief unchecked. `AtomTable` gains a `limit: usize` field defaulted from the constant by both `new()` and `with_common_atoms()`, plus a `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate) fn with_limit(limit: usize) -> Self` so the walls can drive the cap with a table of eight atoms instead of a million. `limit()` loses `const fn` and returns the field (signature otherwise unchanged; callers at `scheduler/mod.rs:1835` and `scheduler/tests.rs:651` keep compiling). Add `is_full()`.

D2 THE FALLIBLE ENTRY POINT. `pub fn try_intern(&self, name: &str) -> Result<Atom, AtomTableFull>` — a new tiny public error type (unit struct or fieldless enum carrying the limit for its `Display`). It is the ONLY path that enforces the cap. RACE-FREE INDEX ISSUE (load-bearing): today's `Entry::Vacant` arm does an unconditional `next_index.fetch_add(1, Relaxed)`. A `len() < limit` pre-check followed by `fetch_add` is a TOCTOU across DashMap shards and would let N racing threads overshoot. The correct shape is a bounded `next_index.fetch_update(Relaxed, Relaxed, |n| ((n as usize) < limit).then(|| n + 1))` INSIDE the Vacant arm (so the name→atom insert stays atomic under the entry guard): `Err` from `fetch_update` means full, no index is burned, and nothing is leaked. Because `limit <= u32::MAX` the same guard also closes the review's `u32` index-wrap concern by construction.

D3 `intern` KEEPS ITS SIGNATURE, GAINS A CONTRACT. `pub fn intern(&self, name: &str) -> Atom` stays for the ~1,378 sites interning compile-time-known names, delegating to the shared insert path WITHOUT the cap. Its doc comment gains a hard, quotable contract: any caller whose `name` derives from process input, peer bytes, or a loaded file MUST use `try_intern`; `intern` is for names fixed in the source. The contract is made durable by the R4 prohibition grep, not by trust.

D4 THE THREE VECTORS, each refusing in its own existing vocabulary:
- BIFs (`gate3_bifs/type_conversion.rs:51` and `:120`): `try_intern`; on `Err` return `Err(Term::atom(Atom::SYSTEM_LIMIT))`. This needs a NEW `Atom::SYSTEM_LIMIT = Self(77)` and a `("system_limit", Atom::SYSTEM_LIMIT)` row APPENDED to `COMMON_ATOMS`. This matches OTP, where `list_to_atom`/`binary_to_atom` on a full table raise a catchable `system_limit`. These BIFs return `Result<Term, Term>`, so no `ExecError` variant and no `beamr-wasm` `reasons.rs` row are involved — confirm that with `cargo check`, do not assume it.
- Distribution (`distribution/etf.rs:627` `decode_atom`): `try_intern`; on `Err` return a NEW `DecodeError::AtomTableFull`. The frame is refused, the error propagates through `ControlError` to the existing frame-rejection path, and the LINK is torn down. THE NODE SURVIVES. `DecodeError` is a public enum (`distribution/etf.rs:35-49`) — the new variant is an exhaustive-match sweep; every downstream match gains an explicit arm.
- Loader: route the atom-chunk intern through `try_intern` and map `Err` onto the existing `LoadError::DecodeError("atom table full".into())` — no new loader type, reusing the same shape as `charge_atom`'s "decode atom budget exhausted". The per-module `MAX_ATOMS_PER_MODULE` budget stays exactly as it is; the global cap is an additional, independent ceiling.

D5 WHAT "HALT LOUDLY" MEANS HERE — a deliberate, stated divergence from ERTS. ERTS `erts_exit`s / crash-dumps when the atom table cannot grow. beamr is an EMBEDDABLE LIBRARY, not a standalone node: aborting the host process on a remote peer's input would be a strictly worse DoS than the leak. beamr's loudness is therefore (i) a typed, non-silent refusal at each of the three seams, never a fallback atom and never a silent no-op; (ii) `erlang:system_info(atom_limit)` reporting the enforced number so the ceiling is observable from Erlang code; (iii) `is_full()` available to embedders. The divergence and its reason must be written into the `ATOM_TABLE_LIMIT` doc comment so a later reader does not "fix" it into an abort.

OQ-A (carved, NOT for this lane; record in the handoff): whether `intern` should eventually be deleted outright in favour of `try_intern` everywhere. That is a ~1,378-site mechanical sweep with real review cost and no additional safety once the untrusted vectors are routed and grep-walled. This brief deliberately does not attempt it.

requirements.title: RED — the cap is inert: three vectors intern past the limit and `limit()` lies
requirements.spec: Per D1: land the limit FIELD, the `#[cfg(test)]` `with_limit` constructor, `is_full()`, and the honest-`limit()` return — with ENFORCEMENT DELIBERATELY ABSENT — plus the four failing assertions. This is a genuine bytes-red, not a compile-red: the walls compile and fail on their assertions.
acceptance: BOUNDED-RED CONSTRAINT (load-bearing): every vector wall runs against a `with_limit(8)` table and interns at most ~16 short names. NO test in this lane may intern toward the real 1,048,576 ceiling, and no test may allocate memory proportional to `ATOM_TABLE_LIMIT`. The defect is demonstrated by asserting the refusal path at a tiny limit, never by exhausting the box.

Leg A (BIF vector): with a `with_limit(8)` table already at its limit, `erlang:binary_to_atom/1` and `erlang:list_to_atom/1` on fresh names are asserted to return `Err(Term::atom(Atom::SYSTEM_LIMIT))`; at current bytes both succeed and the table grows past 8 → RED.

Leg B (distribution vector): `decode_control_addressed` / `decode_term` fed a control frame carrying a fresh remote atom against a full `with_limit(8)` table is asserted to return `DecodeError::AtomTableFull`; at current bytes it decodes successfully and grows the table → RED.
Leg C (loader vector): a module load whose atom chunk carries fresh names against a full `with_limit(8)` table is asserted to fail with `LoadError::DecodeError`; at current bytes it loads → RED.

Leg D (the lie): `AtomTable::new().limit() == ATOM_TABLE_LIMIT`; at current bytes `limit()` returns `u32::MAX as usize` → RED. Paired assertion: `scheduler.atom_limit()` reports the same enforced number.

All four legs live as in-crate unit tests (the `with_limit` constructor is `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate)` and is not visible to `crates/beamr/tests/**`); this placement is deliberate and must be stated in the handoff.

requirements.title: `try_intern` with a race-free bounded index allocation
requirements.spec: Per D2/D3: the new fallible entry point, the `AtomTableFull` error type, the bounded `fetch_update` inside the `Entry::Vacant` arm, and the hardened `intern` doc contract.
acceptance: `try_intern` refuses once the table holds `limit` atoms and returns `Ok` for a name ALREADY interned even at the limit (an existing atom is a lookup, never an insert — a table at its ceiling must not start failing to resolve names it already knows).

The bound is enforced by a single `fetch_update` on `next_index` inside the `Entry::Vacant` arm — no `len()`-then-`fetch_add` TOCTOU, no index burned on refusal, no `Box::leak` performed on a refused name.

CONCURRENCY WALL: eight threads racing distinct fresh names against a `with_limit(64)` table produce EXACTLY 64 interned atoms, every assigned index is `< 64`, no index is assigned twice, and every returned atom resolves to its own name. Ten consecutive isolated runs green.

`intern` keeps its exact signature and behaviour for the ~1,378 existing call sites (workspace compiles with zero changes to them); its doc comment carries the untrusted-input contract naming `try_intern` as the required alternative.
R1 leg D goes GREEN; `erlang:system_info(atom_limit)` reports the enforced ceiling.

requirements.title: Route the three untrusted vectors and mint each refusal in its own vocabulary
requirements.spec: Per D4/D5: BIFs → `system_limit` atom; distribution decoder → `DecodeError::AtomTableFull` → link torn down, node survives; loader → existing `LoadError::DecodeError`. Includes the `COMMON_ATOMS` append and the `DecodeError` exhaustive sweep.
acceptance: `Atom::SYSTEM_LIMIT = Self(77)` and a `("system_limit", Atom::SYSTEM_LIMIT)` row APPENDED as the 78th entry of `COMMON_ATOMS`. Indices 0..=76 are byte-immovable and `with_common_atoms`'s `next_index` store follows `COMMON_ATOMS.len()` as it already does. Any reordering or renumbering of an existing common atom is a STOP.

`bif_binary_to_atom` (`type_conversion.rs:51`) and `bif_list_to_atom` (`:120`) use `try_intern` and return `Err(Term::atom(Atom::SYSTEM_LIMIT))` on refusal — catchable by ordinary Erlang `try`/`catch`, matching OTP. R1 leg A GREEN. `binary_to_existing_atom`/`list_to_existing_atom` are byte-unchanged.

`distribution/etf.rs:627` `decode_atom` uses `try_intern` and returns the new `DecodeError::AtomTableFull`; R1 leg B GREEN. NODE-SURVIVAL leg: with a second live connection open, an atom-flooding peer's frame is refused and its link is marked down while the second connection stays up and the manager keeps serving.

The loader's atom-chunk intern uses `try_intern`, mapping refusal to `LoadError::DecodeError`; R1 leg C GREEN. `MAX_ATOMS_PER_MODULE` and `DecodeBudget::charge_atom` are byte-unchanged — the two ceilings are independent.

EXHAUSTIVE SWEEP: `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` is clean; every downstream `match` on `DecodeError` gains an EXPLICIT `AtomTableFull` arm. Zero `_ =>` catch-alls introduced. Confirm by `cargo check` whether any `ExecError`/`beamr-wasm` `reasons.rs` surface is implicated — the design says no, the build must say no.

requirements.title: Permanent walls — the four legs, the concurrency wall, and the untrusted-intern prohibition grep
requirements.spec: The R1/R2 legs become permanent, joined by a grep wall that pins the D3 contract so a future edit cannot silently reintroduce an uncapped intern on an untrusted path.
acceptance: PROHIBITION GREP (added to the lane's gate evidence and runnable standalone): no bare `.intern(` outside `cfg(test)` in `crates/beamr/src/distribution/etf.rs`, `crates/beamr/src/native/gate3_bifs/**`, or `crates/beamr/src/loader/decode/**` — these are the untrusted-bytes modules and they must use `try_intern`. The grep's rationale is committed alongside it.
The R1 legs A–D and the R2 concurrency wall are permanent tests, not scratch probes, and each is named for the vector it guards.
IDEMPOTENCE WALL: re-interning an existing name at a full table succeeds and returns the same atom (guards against a cap implementation that refuses lookups).

FAIL-FIRST RECORDED: revert the R2 enforcement commit → legs A/B/C and the concurrency wall go red → restore. Revert the R3 BIF routing alone → leg A goes red while B and C stay green (proving the walls are vector-specific, not one coarse assertion) → restore. Both transcripts in the handoff.

boundaries: BOUNDED RED IS ABSOLUTE: every wall runs at a `with_limit(8)`/`with_limit(64)` table. No test may intern toward 1,048,576, allocate proportionally to `ATOM_TABLE_LIMIT`, or demonstrate the leak by actually leaking. The refusal path is the evidence.

NO ABORT: the cap must never `panic!`, `abort`, `exit`, or kill the node/host process. That is a deliberate divergence from ERTS's crash-dump behaviour, justified by beamr being an embeddable library, and it must be recorded in the `ATOM_TABLE_LIMIT` doc comment. A refusal that takes down the VM is a STOP.

`COMMON_ATOMS` IS APPEND-ONLY: indices 0..=76 are immovable (wire encodings, golden vectors and `Atom::` constants depend on them). `system_limit` takes index 77. Reordering, inserting, or renumbering any existing row is a STOP.

`intern` KEEPS ITS SIGNATURE: the ~1,378 existing call sites are NOT mechanically rewritten in this lane. Only the three untrusted vectors move to `try_intern`. Widening to a workspace-wide sweep is OQ-A and out of scope.

SCOPE: this brief CAPS the leak; it does not add atom garbage collection or unloading. `Box::leak` at `atom/table.rs:230` stays — the `&'static str` return of `resolve` depends on it, and changing that is a different, much larger design.

NO KNOB: `ATOM_TABLE_LIMIT` is a documented `const`. No `+t`-equivalent runtime flag, environment variable, embedder setting, or `Scheduler` builder option. `with_limit` is `#[cfg(test)]`-gated and is never public API.

ZERO new `#[allow]` of any kind; no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside `cfg(test)`; no `_ =>` catch-all arms introduced to absorb the new `DecodeError::AtomTableFull` — every downstream match gains an explicit arm.
NO-POLLING: no timed retry, backoff, or spin anywhere in the fix or the walls; the concurrency wall joins its threads, it does not sleep-and-check.

MERGE-ORDER NOTE (not a hard dependency): this lane edits `crates/beamr/src/distribution/etf.rs` at `decode_atom` (`:627`); RF-003 edits the same file at `read_dist_message` (`:146-152`) and adds a module-level constant. Different functions, textual-conflict risk only — whichever lands second rebases.
verification:
PIN-SHIFT RE-VERIFY FIRST, BEFORE ANY EDIT: re-confirm at the actual build base (not at a0359a2) that `atom/table.rs:220` `intern` still `fetch_add`s at `:228` and `Box::leak`s at `:230`; that `limit()` at `:266-270` still returns `u32::MAX as usize`; that `COMMON_ATOMS` still has exactly 77 rows ending at `Atom::INFINITY = Self(76)`; that `distribution/etf.rs:627` `decode_atom` still calls `intern` unconditionally and `control_link.rs:267` still reaches it via `decode_term`; that `gate3_bifs/type_conversion.rs:51` and `:120` still intern; and that `system_limit` still appears nowhere in the tree. Record any drift in the handoff before starting.

GATE BAR — the full release battery from `gates.json` at the FINAL head, all five legs green in one sitting: (1) `cargo fmt --all --check`; (2) `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` for BOTH closures, fresh (Compiling lines visible); (3) `cargo test --workspace`; (4) `cargo check -p beamr-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --locked`; (5) the wasm-tests leg (`wasm-bindgen-test-runner` + `cargo test --manifest-path crates/beamr-wasm/Cargo.toml --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --locked`). Plus the R4 prohibition grep and 10× isolation on the concurrency wall.

FAIL-FIRST DEMONSTRATION at the final head: revert the R2 enforcement commit → R1 legs A/B/C and the concurrency wall go red → restore. Then revert only the R3 BIF routing → leg A red, legs B and C still green → restore. Recorded with exact assertion text.

HANDOFF must carry: the CONFIRMED provenance of 1_048_576 against the `erl` manual (or a corrected value with its citation), the `cargo check` result for whether `ExecError`/`beamr-wasm` `reasons.rs` were implicated (design says no), the full list of downstream `DecodeError` match sites that gained an arm, the landed `Atom::SYSTEM_LIMIT` index, and the confirmed re-pinned file:lines as built.
